🪖 HELMET IMPACT TEST

ISI Standard vs Ordinary vs No Helmet

ℹ️ Disclaimer & Test Info

The same weight is dropped on three watermelons (standing in for a head): one with no helmet, one with an ordinary helmet, and one with a certified helmet.

Damage shown in the demonstration

Weight droppedNo helmetOrdinary helmetCertified helmet
5 kg100%15% (minor)0%
10 kg100%40% (moderate)0%
25 kg100%85% (critical)0%
50 kg100%100% (fatal)15% (minor dent)

What it shows

  • No helmet: 100% fatal in every case.
  • Ordinary helmet: damage grows with weight, from minor to fatal.
  • Certified helmet: fully protected at lower weights; only a minor dent at 50 kg, with the inside still safe.
  • Takeaway: a certified helmet absorbs impact far better.

Disclaimer: This is an illustrative demonstration, not a laboratory test. The watermelon only represents a head, and the percentages are simplified figures for explanation. They are not real test results, medical advice, or a guarantee of safety. Real accidents vary widely and no helmet can protect in every situation.

Helmet safety standards differ by country (for example ISI/BIS in India, DOT in the USA, ECE 22 in Europe, AS/NZS 1698 in Australia and New Zealand). Always wear a helmet that meets the standard required where you live, fitted properly and with the strap fastened.
